text: Cream is homogenised and soured with a mesophilic starter (O- or DL-type) at room temperature overnight until it gels at pH 4.5–4.8. The gel is warmed and the whey is spun or drained off; the cold curd is salted and packed, or hot-packed for a longer shelf life.

steps.note: A little rennet may also be added to the cream.
The curd is stirred and heated to 50–70 °C, then drained: in cloth bags overnight at 75–90 °C, in a centrifugal separator at 70–85 °C, or by ultrafiltration at 50–55 °C.
A stabiliser under 0.5 % is added with the salt, such as locust bean, guar, xanthan, alginate or carrageenan.

processing.text: Mesophilic starter, O-type (acid only) or DL-type (with the two aroma organisms). A faster set is 31 °C for about 5 h with 5 % starter.
